headline: Medium risk: AutoGPT can write and egress while langchain4j is a local library, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and workflow-conflict exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and call agent protocol APIs, so attacker-controlled content can reach its instruction stream. langchain4j is a library with no direct runtime surface shown, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than directly documented. The shared filesystem path makes prompt injection plausible in default use, but not proven high.
conditions: IF AutoGPT ingests files or agent-protocol messages produced by langchain4j without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the two are bridged through a shared workspace or copied prompts, attacker text can become instructions.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every file or message before AutoGPT reads it.
Restrict AutoGPT to a dedicated input directory.
Review any langchain4j-generated text before passing it to AutoGPT.
Disable automatic execution of instructions found in files.
requires-engineering: add parser hardening and content-sanitization gates.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress, so it can move local content outward. langchain4j itself shows no egress, but as a library it can still feed data into AutoGPT workflows. No sensitive data class is listed, so the blast radius is bounded, yet the shared workspace plus outbound-capable AutoGPT creates a default leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace, AutoGPT can read and transmit them through allowlisted egress.
IF langchain4j passes file contents into AutoGPT prompts, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory.
Use separate OS users for the two components.
Block AutoGPT from reading directories containing secrets.
Audit outbound destinations on AutoGPT's allowlist.
requires-engineering: add DLP or redaction before any outbound call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem; langchain4j is a framework that may orchestrate overlapping mutable resources. The profiles do not show locking or isolated workspaces, so concurrent writes or state corruption are plausible. Uncertainty about langchain4j's runtime role pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both components write to the same directory or git checkout, file clobbering can occur.
IF langchain4j is used to coordinate the same mutable resource AutoGPT edits, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple lock file.
Avoid sharing a git checkout between them.
Run one component at a time during edits.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate autonomous outputs and langchain4j can consume them as part of an application flow. Because no verification or human approval step is shown, B may treat A's text as authoritative. The pair is not documented as a safe checked pipeline, so the default risk is a mistaken action chain rather than a guaranteed harmful action.
conditions: IF langchain4j forwards AutoGPT output into downstream actions without validation, errors can cascade.
IF AutoGPT fabricates facts that langchain4j renders or acts on, the downstream result can be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action.
Require schema validation on AutoGPT outputs.
Compare outputs against a second source before use.
Log and diff each handoff between the two.
requires-engineering: add automated verification and rollback for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are listed for either agent. AutoGPT's allowlisted egress and langchain4j's no-egress profile do not by themselves create a compliance breach in the rubric's terms. With no compliance-specific mismatch evidence, the pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent, reassess residency and retention.
IF a deployment adds jurisdictional or certification constraints, the compliance profile changes.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of the pair until reviewed.
Record retention settings for both components.
requires-engineering: map jurisdictions and certifications for the full workflow.
